rationale: Split by exact reuse of five comparator-accepted DAG declarations. Four are the substantive obligations of the supplied proof: the test-form pull-back (Notation and step 1(a)), the mass scaling (step 5), the integrality transport (step 6) and the H^k change of variables (step 7). The fifth, the tangent-space invariance used inside step 6, is the dependency of the integrality child. Each already exists in another branch with a frozen type that is string-identical to the one proposed here: cmcdt_dil_pullback_testForm, cmcdt_dil_mass_eq, cmcdt_dil_isIntegerMultiplicity, euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables and dtc_approxTangent_dilation. All five are status accepted with candidate commits (eb59ffc0, 836f8d74, fd2b8d73, 22204a6d, 2b0c5140). The runtime rule (_existing_lean_name_problem / _solve_children) maps them onto the existing accepted nodes, so they need no new worker. The four substantive pieces are long analytic arguments (about 300 Lean lines in the accepted proofs). Their hypothesis form Y(omega) = X(eta) whenever eta = affinePullbackForm (lam.id) 0 omega is exactly the defining property of the parent's dil. Without the split, the parent would have to re-prove them. With it, the parent's remaining work is the mechanical assembly of steps 2-4 and 8, which uses only SimonGMT and these children. (a) Definition: dil k lam X := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward (lam.id) 0 (proper, Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero) X for lam /= 0, and X otherwise. Then dil k lam X (omega) = X(eta) whenever eta = affinePullbackForm (lam.id) 0 omega (affinePushforward_apply, restrictDomain_apply, Subtype.ext). (1) Subtraction holds pointwise. (2) Inversion: apply pullback_testform twice, then lam^k (lam^-1)^k = 1 and lam^-1 lam x = x. (3) Mass: mass child with Y := dil k lam X. (4) IM: integer_multiplicity child with Y := dil k lam X. (5) Boundary: SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward (step 1(c), Simon 2.24(1)). (6) Vanishing: SimonGMT tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset (step 1(a)); if lam x lies in tsupport omega with x in E, then lam x lies in tsupport omega and in lam E, contradicting the disjointness. (7) Explicit action: pullback_testform gives eta with the pointwise formula, and the defining property gives dil k lam X (omega) = X(eta). (8) Change of variables: part (iii) of hausdorff_change_of_variables with c = lam and M = lam A; the preimage of lam A under x -> lam x is A (Set.preimage_image_eq, smul_right_injective), so the integral of g(lam z) over A equals lam^-k times the integral of g over lam A; multiply by lam^k. Verification in the contract scope (import GMT.Ch07.Submission, namespace GMT.Ch07, opens of the frozen contract): the five child types and the parent type elaborate as comparator challenges. An assembly theorem taking the five child types (DAG strings, byte-identical) as hypotheses proves the frozen parent type with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; the approx_tangent hypothesis is unused at parent level and needed only inside integer_multiplicity. A full chain was also compiled: the accepted proofs of the five declarations (from the accepted commit fba5d30a of cmcdt_dilation_pushforward) plus this assembly prove Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_dilation with the same three axioms. Dependencies are acyclic: mass <- pullback_testform; integer_multiplicity <- pullback_testform, hausdorff_change_of_variables, approx_tangent.

subproblems.title: Dilation pull-back of a test form: affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω is a test form with value λ^k ω(λx)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and λ ∈ ℝ with λ ≠ 0, and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ k, a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^P = Euclid P with compact support. Put L := λ·id = lam • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) and δ_λ^#ω := affinePullbackForm L 0 ω (SimonGMT). This is the k-form x ↦ (ω(0 + Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L, i.e. (δ_λ^#ω)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = ω(λx)(λv_1, …, λv_k). Then there is η ∈ TestFormOn univ k whose underlying differential form equals δ_λ^#ω and which satisfies η(x) = λ^k • ω(λ • x), as k-covectors, for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (lam : ℝ), lam ≠ 0 → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = affinePullbackForm (lam • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P)) 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid P, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = lam ^ k • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (lam • x)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph and step 1(a) of the parent proof. There (δ_λ^#ω)(x) = ω(λx) ∘ (λ·id) = λ^k ω(λx), and δ_λ^#ω is C^∞ with compact support λ⁻¹·tsupport ω, hence a test form. This is the pull-back f^#ω of Simon 6.2.23 for f = δ_λ (chapter-06.txt lines 404–410).

Notation: L := λ·id. For a k-form ω, affinePullbackForm L 0 ω is the form x ↦ (ω(0 + Lx)).compContinuousLinearMap L (SimonGMT Chapter06/AffineCurrentPushforward.lean). TestFormOn univ k is the set of k-forms that are test forms (IsTestForm: C^∞ with compact support) with tsupport ⊆ univ.

1. Properness. For every x ∈ ℝ^P, 0 + Lx = λx. Since λ ≠ 0, x ↦ λx is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ λ⁻¹y (Mathlib Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ), hence a proper map (Homeomorph.isProperMap). The map x ↦ 0 + Lx agrees with it at every point, so it is proper.

2. Test form. ω is C^∞ with compact support (first component of its membership proof). The form affinePullbackForm L 0 ω is the composite of the C^∞ map x ↦ ω(0 + Lx) with the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap L on k-covectors, so it is C^∞ (SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm). Its topological support is contained in the preimage of tsupport ω under x ↦ 0 + Lx (SimonGMT tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset). This preimage is compact because the map is proper (step 1) and tsupport ω is compact. A topological support is closed, and a closed subset of a compact set is compact, so the support is compact. SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm L 0, applied with the properness of step 1, packages these two facts. The inclusion tsupport ⊆ univ is trivial. Hence η := ⟨affinePullbackForm L 0 ω, (test form, tsupport ⊆ univ)⟩ ∈ TestFormOn univ k. Its underlying form is affinePullbackForm L 0 ω by construction, which proves the first conjunct.

3. Pointwise formula. Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and v = (v_1, …, v_k) ∈ (ℝ^P)^k. By the definitions of affinePullbackForm and compContinuousLinearMap, and since 0 + Lx = λx: η(x)(v) = ω(λx)(Lv_1, …, Lv_k) = ω(λx)(λv_1, …, λv_k). The covector ω(λx) is a continuous alternating, hence multilinear, map. So ω(λx)(c_1v_1, …, c_kv_k) = (∏_{i ∈ Fin k} c_i)·ω(λx)(v_1, …, v_k) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ). With every c_i = λ, ∏_{i ∈ Fin k} λ = λ^k (Fin.prod_const). Hence η(x)(v) = λ^k·ω(λx)(v) = (λ^k • ω(λx))(v). For k = 0 the product is empty and equals 1 = λ^0, so the formula reads η(x) = ω(λx).

4. As v was arbitrary, η(x) = λ^k • ω(λ • x) as continuous alternating maps (extensionality), for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Together with step 2 this proves both conjuncts. ∎
proof_key_steps: For λ ≠ 0 the map x ↦ 0 + (λ·id)x = λx is a homeomorphism (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero), hence proper.

SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm: the pull-back of a test form along a proper affine map is a test form; tsupport ⊆ univ is trivial, so η := ⟨affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω, _⟩ ∈ TestFormOn univ k, with the required underlying form by construction.
Multilinearity of ω(λx) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ, Fin.prod_const): ω(λx)(λv_1, …, λv_k) = λ^k ω(λx)(v), so η(x) = λ^k • ω(λx) for every x, including k = 0.

subproblems.title: Change of variables for Hⁿ under x ↦ cx (c > 0): image measure, lower and Bochner integrals over T⁻¹(M)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and c ∈ ℝ with c > 0. Let T(x) := c·x on ℝ^P = Euclid P, let Hⁿ := μHE[n] (normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure), and let M ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set. Then: (i) the image measure of Hⁿ⌞T⁻¹(M) under T (Measure.map) equals ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ⌞M; (ii) for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_{T⁻¹(M)} g(cz) dHⁿ(z) = ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·∫⁻_M g dHⁿ; (iii) for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{T⁻¹(M)} g(cz) dHⁿ(z) = (c⁻¹)^n·∫_M g dHⁿ (Bochner integrals). No measurability or integrability hypotheses are assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → ∀ M : Set (Euclid P), Measure.map (fun x : Euclid P => c • x) (μHE[n].restrict ((fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M)) = ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹ ^ n) • μHE[n].restrict M ∧ (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ z in (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M, g (c • z) ∂μHE[n] = ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹ ^ n) * ∫⁻ y in M, g y ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ z in (fun x => c • x) ⁻¹' M, g (c • z) ∂μHE[n] = c⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ y in M, g y ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof, with the Hausdorff scaling Hᵏ(δ_λ(A)) = λ^kHᵏ(A) of step 6. The image measure of μHE[k] under δ_λ is λ^{−k}μHE[k], δ_λ is a measurable equivalence, restriction commutes with taking the image, and the change of variables holds for arbitrary integrands. Here this is stated for c = λ. The parent obtains ∫_{λA} g dHᵏ = λ^k∫_A g(λx) dHᵏ(x) from (iii) with M = λA, since T⁻¹(λA) = A.

Notation: T(x) := cx; ν⌞E := ν.restrict E. Throughout c > 0, so c ≠ 0 and c⁻¹ > 0.

1. T is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with inverse x ↦ c⁻¹x (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero c), hence a measurable embedding for the Borel σ-algebra (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding). In particular T is measurable and injective.

2. Image of Hⁿ. Let B ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then (T_#Hⁿ)(B) = Hⁿ(T⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, T measurable, B measurable), and T⁻¹(B) = {x : cx ∈ B} = c⁻¹·B (Set.preimage_smul₀). The Euclidean Hausdorff measure scales as Hⁿ(r·S) = ‖r‖₊^n·Hⁿ(S) for every set S and every r ≠ 0 (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). This follows from hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ because μHE[n] is a constant multiple of μH[n]. With r = c⁻¹: Hⁿ(c⁻¹B) = ‖c⁻¹‖₊^n·Hⁿ(B). Since c⁻¹ > 0 we have ‖c⁻¹‖₊ = c⁻¹, so the factor ‖c⁻¹‖₊^n, read in [0, ∞], equals ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n). Hence (T_#Hⁿ)(B) = ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ(B) for every Borel B. Measures that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext), so T_#Hⁿ = ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ.

3. Proof of (i). For a measurable embedding T, any measure ν and any set M (no measurability of M is needed), (T_#ν)⌞M = T_#(ν⌞T⁻¹(M)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). Take ν = Hⁿ and use step 2: T_#(Hⁿ⌞T⁻¹(M)) = (ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ)⌞M = ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ⌞M. The last step holds because restriction commutes with multiplying a measure by a constant (Measure.restrict_smul).

4. Proof of (ii). For a measurable embedding T, every measure ν and every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (measurable or not), ∫⁻ g d(T_#ν) = ∫⁻ (g ∘ T) dν (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map). Take ν = Hⁿ⌞T⁻¹(M) and use (i): ∫⁻_{T⁻¹(M)} g(cz) dHⁿ(z) = ∫⁻ g d(T_#(Hⁿ⌞T⁻¹(M))) = ∫⁻ g d(ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ⌞M) = ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·∫⁻_M g dHⁿ. The last step is linearity of the lower integral in the measure (lintegral_smul_measure).

5. Proof of (iii). For a measurable embedding T, every measure ν and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ g d(T_#ν) = ∫ (g ∘ T) dν (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). No integrability hypothesis is needed: g is T_#ν-integrable iff g ∘ T is ν-integrable, and both Bochner integrals are 0 otherwise. Take ν = Hⁿ⌞T⁻¹(M) and use (i) and ∫ g d(a·μ) = a.toReal·∫ g dμ for a ∈ [0, ∞] (integral_smul_measure): ∫_{T⁻¹(M)} g(cz) dHⁿ(z) = (ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)).toReal·∫_M g dHⁿ = (c⁻¹)^n·∫_M g dHⁿ. The last step holds because (c⁻¹)^n ≥ 0 gives (ENNReal.ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)).toReal = (c⁻¹)^n (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). This proves (i), (ii) and (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: T(x) = cx is a homeomorphism, hence a measurable embedding of ℝ^P.
T⁻¹(B) = c⁻¹B and Hⁿ(c⁻¹B) = (c⁻¹)^nHⁿ(B) (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀) give T_#Hⁿ = ofReal((c⁻¹)^n)·Hⁿ.
MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map and integral_map, with linearity of the integrals in the measure, give (ii) and (iii) for arbitrary g.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent spaces are invariant under the dilations η_{x,λ}, λ > 0
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P, x, y ∈ ℝ^P, λ ∈ ℝ with λ > 0, and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. Let η := dilation x λ, η(w) = −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹w (Simon's η_{x,λ}(w) = λ⁻¹(w − x)). Suppose Q is the n-dimensional approximate tangent space of M at y in the sense of SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q. That is, dim Q = n, and for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺, where blowUpMap y r w = r⁻¹(w − y) and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then Q is also the n-dimensional approximate tangent space of η(M) at η(y), i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η '' M) (η(y)) Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x y : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < lam → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (dilation x lam '' M) (dilation x lam y) Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof: the approximate tangent space of λM at λx equals that of M at x, because blowUpMap (λx) r '' (λM) = blowUpMap x (r/λ) '' M, so the defining limits coincide. Here this is written for a general dilation η = η_{x,λ}. The parent's map δ_λ(w) = λw is η_{0,λ⁻¹}: dilation 0 λ⁻¹ w = −(λ·0) + λw = λw, with λ⁻¹ > 0. Definition: Simon Ch. 3, 1.4, formalized as SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.

1. Dimension. The condition dim Q = n involves neither the set nor the base point. It holds for M at y, so it holds for η(M) at η(y).

2. Set identity. For every w ∈ ℝ^P, η(w) − η(y) = (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹w) − (−λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y) = λ⁻¹(w − y). Hence for every r ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap(η(y), r)(η(w)) = r⁻¹·λ⁻¹(w − y) = (λr)⁻¹(w − y) = blowUpMap(y, λr)(w). This uses (λr)⁻¹ = λ⁻¹r⁻¹, which holds in ℝ for every r, including r = 0 with the convention 0⁻¹ = 0. The image of an image is the image under the composite, so blowUpMap(η(y), r) '' (η '' M) = blowUpMap(y, λr) '' M for every r ∈ ℝ.

3. Fix a compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ and put g(s) := ∫_{blowUpMap(y, s) '' M} f dHⁿ. By step 2, ∫_{blowUpMap(η(y), r) '' (η '' M)} f dHⁿ = g(λr) for every r. The domains of integration coincide and the integrand and the measure are the same, so no integrability is needed for this equality.

4. Limit. The map r ↦ λr sends the filter r → 0⁺ into the filter s → 0⁺. It is continuous with value 0 at 0, so λr → 0 as r → 0; and λr > 0 whenever r > 0, because λ > 0. By hypothesis g(s) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as s → 0⁺. Composing the two limits, g(λr) → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺. By step 3, ∫_{blowUpMap(η(y), r) '' (η '' M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺.

5. Since f was arbitrary, steps 1 and 4 together say exactly HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (η '' M) (η(y)) Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: dim Q = n does not depend on the set or base point.
η(w) − η(y) = λ⁻¹(w − y), hence blowUpMap(η(y), r) '' η(M) = blowUpMap(y, λr) '' M for every r.
The rescaled integrals of η(M) at η(y) and scale r equal those of M at y and scale λr; r ↦ λr maps r → 0⁺ to s → 0⁺, so the limit transfers.

subproblems.title: Mass scaling under the dilation push-forward: M(δ_{λ#}X) = λ^k M(X)
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, λ ∈ ℝ with λ > 0, and X, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. Assume Y(ω) = X(η) for all test forms ω, η ∈ TestFormOn univ k whose underlying forms satisfy η = affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω, i.e. η = δ_λ^#ω, so that Y = δ_{λ#}X is the push-forward of X by δ_λ(x) = λx. Then Y.mass = ENNReal.ofReal(λ^k)·X.mass in [0, ∞]. Here T.mass = T.massOn univ is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over the test forms ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k with tsupport ω ⊆ univ and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (SimonGMT massAdmissibleOn univ k univ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → ∀ X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = affinePullbackForm (lam • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P)) 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) → Y ω = X η) → Y.mass = ENNReal.ofReal (lam ^ k) * X.mass
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof. There ω ↦ λ^{−k}δ_λ^#ω is a bijection of the admissible forms {|ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} onto itself, with inverse η ↦ λ^kδ_{λ⁻¹}^#η, by 1(d) and 1(e). Hence M(δ_{λ#}X) = ENNReal.ofReal(λ^k)·M(X), using ENNReal.ofReal(ab) = ENNReal.ofReal(a)·ENNReal.ofReal(b) for a ≥ 0 and the fact that multiplication by a constant commutes with suprema in [0, ∞]. The norm identity 1(e) is used in the form supplied by the sibling pullback_testform: λ^{−k}(δ_λ^#ω)(x) = ω(λx) as covectors, so the Euclidean coefficient norms agree pointwise. This is the change of scale that Simon uses before 5.3 (chapter-06.txt lines 1458–1460).

Notation: |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, and ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal. 𝒜 := massAdmissibleOn univ k univ = {ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k : tsupport ω ⊆ univ and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}. M(T) = T.mass = T.massOn univ = sSup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒜}, and ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M(T) for ω ∈ 𝒜 (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since λ > 0 we have λ ≠ 0, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0 and λ^k > 0. PT is the sibling pullback_testform: for μ ≠ 0 and every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k there is η ∈ TestFormOn univ k with η = affinePullbackForm (μ·id) 0 ω as forms and η(x) = μ^k • ω(μx) for all x. Currents are ℝ-linear on the submodule TestFormOn univ k (T(cω) = c·T(ω)). Two elements of TestFormOn univ k with equal underlying forms are equal (Subtype.ext).

1. Upper bound M(Y) ≤ ofReal(λ^k)·M(X). Since M(Y) is a supremum, it suffices to fix ω ∈ 𝒜 and show ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(λ^k)·M(X).
 (a) Let η be given by PT for μ = λ and ω. By the hypothesis, Y(ω) = X(η).
 (b) Put η' := (λ^k)⁻¹·η ∈ TestFormOn univ k. For every x, η'(x) = (λ^k)⁻¹·λ^k·ω(λx) = ω(λx), so |η'(x)| = |ω(λx)| ≤ 1; also tsupport η' ⊆ univ. Hence η' ∈ 𝒜 and ofReal(X(η')) ≤ M(X).
 (c) η = λ^k·η' in TestFormOn univ k, so X(η) = λ^k·X(η') by linearity. As λ^k ≥ 0, ofReal(λ^k·X(η')) = ofReal(λ^k)·ofReal(X(η')) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul).
 (d) Therefore ofReal(Y(ω)) = ofReal(X(η)) = ofReal(λ^k)·ofReal(X(η')) ≤ ofReal(λ^k)·M(X), by monotonicity of multiplication in [0, ∞].

2. Lower bound ofReal(λ^k)·M(X) ≤ M(Y). Multiplication by a constant commutes with suprema in [0, ∞] (ENNReal.mul_sSup). So ofReal(λ^k)·M(X) = sup_{η ∈ 𝒜} ofReal(λ^k)·ofReal(X(η)). Fix η ∈ 𝒜; it suffices to show ofReal(λ^k)·ofReal(X(η)) ≤ M(Y).
 (a) Let ζ be given by PT for μ = λ⁻¹ and η, so ζ(y) = (λ⁻¹)^k·η(λ⁻¹y) for all y. Put ω := λ^k·ζ ∈ TestFormOn univ k. Then for every y, ω(y) = λ^k·(λ⁻¹)^k·η(λ⁻¹y) = (λλ⁻¹)^k·η(λ⁻¹y) = η(λ⁻¹y).
 (b) Hence |ω(y)| = |η(λ⁻¹y)| ≤ 1 for every y, and tsupport ω ⊆ univ. So ω ∈ 𝒜 and ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ M(Y).
 (c) Let η₂ be given by PT for μ = λ and ω: η₂ = affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω as forms. For all x, η₂(x) = λ^k·ω(λx) = λ^k·η(λ⁻¹λx) = λ^k·η(x). Thus η₂ = λ^k·η in TestFormOn univ k (Subtype.ext, funext).
 (d) By the hypothesis applied to ω and η₂, and by linearity, Y(ω) = X(η₂) = X(λ^k·η) = λ^k·X(η). So ofReal(λ^k)·ofReal(X(η)) = ofReal(λ^k·X(η)) = ofReal(Y(ω)) ≤ M(Y).

3. By 1, 2 and antisymmetry of ≤ on [0, ∞], Y.mass = ofReal(λ^k)·X.mass. The argument is uniform in k, including k = 0 (λ^0 = 1). It uses no finiteness of M(X): both sides may be ∞, since if M(X) = ∞ then step 2 gives M(Y) = ∞ because ofReal(λ^k) ≠ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Upper bound: for admissible ω, let η = δ_λ^#ω (pullback_testform). Then (λ^k)⁻¹η(x) = ω(λx), so (λ^k)⁻¹η is admissible and Y(ω) = X(η) = λ^kX((λ^k)⁻¹η) ≤ λ^kM(X).
Lower bound: for admissible η, ω := λ^kδ_{λ⁻¹}^#η satisfies ω(y) = η(λ⁻¹y), so ω is admissible; and δ_λ^#ω = λ^kη, giving λ^kX(η) = Y(ω) ≤ M(Y).
ENNReal.mul_sSup and ENNReal.ofReal_mul turn the two bounds into Y.mass = ofReal(λ^k)·X.mass (le_antisymm), with no finiteness assumption.

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity is preserved by the dilation push-forward δ_{λ#}, λ > 0
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, λ ∈ ℝ with λ > 0, and X, Y ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k. Assume Y(ω) = X(η) for all test forms ω, η ∈ TestFormOn univ k whose underlying forms satisfy η = affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω, i.e. Y = δ_{λ#}X for δ_λ(x) = λx. Suppose X is integer multiplicity: some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in univ of degree k (contract structure IMRep univ k) represents X, i.e. X(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k, where Hᵏ = μHE[k]. Then Y is integer multiplicity. In fact the triple (λM, θ(λ⁻¹·), ξ(λ⁻¹·)) is an IMRep in univ of degree k that represents Y. This holds in every degree k, including k = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → ∀ X Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (∀ ω η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = affinePullbackForm (lam • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P)) 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) → Y ω = X η) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (Simon 3.3/3.9 for the linear isomorphism δ_λ; chapter-06.txt lines 766–790). There R' := (λM, θ(λ⁻¹·), ξ(λ⁻¹·)) is shown to be an IMRep, with R'.action(ω) = λ^k∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(λx)) dHᵏ(x) = X(δ_λ^#ω) = δ_{λ#}X(ω). This uses the scaling of Hᵏ and the dilation invariance of approximate tangent spaces.

Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]; ν⌞E := ν.restrict E; δ_μ(x) := μx; c₀ := ENNReal.ofReal((λ⁻¹)^k). Since (λ⁻¹)^k > 0, we have 0 < c₀ < ∞. Siblings used:
- PT (pullback_testform): for μ ≠ 0 and every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k there is η ∈ TestFormOn univ k with η = affinePullbackForm (μ·id) 0 ω as forms and η(x) = μ^k • ω(μx) for all x.
- CV (hausdorff_change_of_variables): for c > 0 and any set S ⊆ ℝ^P: (i) (δ_c)_#(Hᵏ⌞δ_c⁻¹(S)) = ofReal((c⁻¹)^k)·Hᵏ⌞S; (ii) ∫⁻_{δ_c⁻¹(S)} g(cz) dHᵏ(z) = ofReal((c⁻¹)^k)·∫⁻_S g dHᵏ for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]; (iii) ∫_{δ_c⁻¹(S)} g(cz) dHᵏ(z) = (c⁻¹)^k·∫_S g dHᵏ for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ.
- AT (approx_tangent): for μ > 0, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q implies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (dilation x μ '' M) (dilation x μ y) Q.

Let R = (M, θ, ξ) : IMRep univ k represent X, i.e. X(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k. Define M' := δ_{λ⁻¹}⁻¹(M) = {y : λ⁻¹y ∈ M}, θ'(y) := θ(λ⁻¹y) and ξ'(y) := ξ(λ⁻¹y).

0. Preliminaries.
 (a) M' = δ_λ(M) = λM. If x ∈ M then λ⁻¹(λx) = x ∈ M; if y ∈ M' then y = λ(λ⁻¹y) with λ⁻¹y ∈ M. Moreover δ_λ⁻¹(δ_{λ⁻¹}⁻¹(S)) = S for every set S, since λ⁻¹(λx) = x. In particular δ_λ⁻¹(M') = M and δ_λ⁻¹(M' ∩ K) = M ∩ δ_λ⁻¹(K) for every K.
 (b) δ_λ is a homeomorphism (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ), hence a measurable embedding.
 (c) CV with c = λ and S = M', rewritten by (a), gives: (i) (δ_λ)_#(Hᵏ⌞M) = c₀·Hᵏ⌞M'; (iii) ∫_M g(λz) dHᵏ(z) = (λ⁻¹)^k·∫_{M'} g dHᵏ for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ.
 (d) A.e. transfer: if p(λx) holds for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. x, then p(y) holds for Hᵏ⌞M'-a.e. y. By (b) and MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff, p holds a.e. for (δ_λ)_#(Hᵏ⌞M), which equals c₀·Hᵏ⌞M' by (c)(i). Since c₀ ≠ 0, holding a.e. for c₀·ν is the same as holding a.e. for ν (Measure.ae_ennreal_smul_measure_iff).
 (e) dilation 0 λ⁻¹ = δ_λ: dilation 0 μ w = −(μ⁻¹·0) + μ⁻¹w = μ⁻¹w, and (λ⁻¹)⁻¹ = λ.

1. R' := (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in univ of degree k. We verify every field.
 - Borel carrier: M' is the preimage of the Borel set M under the continuous, hence measurable, map δ_{λ⁻¹}.
 - M' ⊆ univ trivially.
 - Countably k-rectifiable: R.rectifiable gives M₀ with Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝ^k → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ), each Lipschitz with some constant K_j, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j. Let M₀' := δ_{λ⁻¹}⁻¹(M₀) = λ·M₀ and F_j' := δ_λ ∘ F_j. First, Hᵏ(λ·M₀) = ‖λ‖₊^k·Hᵏ(M₀) = 0 (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, valid for every set). Second, F_j' is Lipschitz with constant ‖λ‖₊K_j (lipschitzWith_smul composed with F_j). Third, for y ∈ M' we have λ⁻¹y ∈ M. Either λ⁻¹y ∈ M₀, and then y ∈ M₀'; or λ⁻¹y = F_j(z) for some j and z, and then y = λF_j(z) = F_j'(z). Hence M' ⊆ M₀' ∪ ⋃_j range F_j'.
 - θ' = θ ∘ δ_{λ⁻¹} is measurable (a composition of measurable maps) and ℕ-valued. For y ∈ M', θ'(y) = θ(λ⁻¹y) > 0 because λ⁻¹y ∈ M.
 - Local integrability: let K be compact (K ⊆ univ). Apply CV(ii) with c = λ and S = M' ∩ K, using δ_λ⁻¹(M' ∩ K) = M ∩ δ_λ⁻¹(K) from (a) and θ'(λz) = θ(z). This gives ∫⁻_{M ∩ δ_λ⁻¹(K)} θ dHᵏ = c₀·∫⁻_{M' ∩ K} θ' dHᵏ. The set δ_λ⁻¹(K) = λ⁻¹K is compact, being the preimage of a compact set under the homeomorphism δ_λ. So the left side is finite by R.locallyIntegrable_mult. If ∫⁻_{M' ∩ K} θ' dHᵏ were ∞, the right side would be c₀·∞ = ∞ (as c₀ ≠ 0), a contradiction. So ∫⁻_{M' ∩ K} θ' dHᵏ ≠ ∞.
 - A.e. strong measurability of ξ': ξ' ∘ δ_λ = ξ, as ξ'(λx) = ξ(λ⁻¹λx) = ξ(x), and ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M. By MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff, ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for (δ_λ)_#(Hᵏ⌞M) = c₀·Hᵏ⌞M'. Since c₀ ≠ 0, Hᵏ⌞M' is absolutely continuous with respect to c₀·Hᵏ⌞M' (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_smul). So ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M' (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac).
 - Orientation: by (d), it suffices that for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M' (λx) Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ'(λx)) Q. By R.orients, for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. For such x, ξ'(λx) = ξ(λ⁻¹λx) = ξ(x), so the orientation condition carries over. Also AT with base point 0, scale μ = λ⁻¹ > 0 and point x gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (dilation 0 λ⁻¹ '' M) (dilation 0 λ⁻¹ x) Q. By (e) and (a), dilation 0 λ⁻¹ '' M = δ_λ(M) = M' and dilation 0 λ⁻¹ x = λx.

2. R' represents Y. Fix ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k, and let η be given by PT for μ = λ and ω: η = affinePullbackForm (λ·id) 0 ω as forms and η(x) = λ^k • ω(λx) for all x. By the hypothesis and since R represents X,
 Y(ω) = X(η) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)) dHᵏ(x) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(λ^k • ω(λx)) dHᵏ(x) = λ^k·∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(λx)) dHᵏ(x).
 The last two steps use linearity of the continuous linear functional ξ(x) and pulling a constant out of the Bochner integral (integral_const_mul, valid without integrability). Now apply (c)(iii) to g(y) := θ'(y)·ξ'(y)(ω(y)). Since g(λz) = θ(z)·ξ(z)(ω(λz)),
 ∫_M θ(z)·ξ(z)(ω(λz)) dHᵏ(z) = (λ⁻¹)^k·∫_{M'} θ'(y)·ξ'(y)(ω(y)) dHᵏ(y) = (λ⁻¹)^k·R'.action ω.
 Hence Y(ω) = λ^k·(λ⁻¹)^k·R'.action ω = (λλ⁻¹)^k·R'.action ω = R'.action ω.

3. Therefore R' represents Y, and Y is integer multiplicity with witness R'. Nothing in the argument depends on k, so it holds in every degree, including k = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: New triple: M' = δ_{λ⁻¹}⁻¹(M) = λM, θ' = θ(λ⁻¹·), ξ' = ξ(λ⁻¹·); M' is Borel, and θ' is measurable, ℕ-valued and positive on M'.
Rectifiability: λM₀ is Hᵏ-null (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀), the maps λF_j are Lipschitz, and they cover M'.
Change of variables (hausdorff_change_of_variables, c = λ): (δ_λ)_#(Hᵏ⌞M) = λ^{-k}Hᵏ⌞M'. This gives local integrability of θ', a.e. strong measurability of ξ', and the a.e. transfer from M to M'.
Approximate tangent planes are dilation invariant (approx_tangent with dilation 0 λ⁻¹ = δ_λ), so ξ'(λx) = ξ(x) orients T_{λx}M'.
Representation: Y(ω) = X(δ_λ^#ω) = λ^k∫_M θξ(ω(λ·)) dHᵏ = λ^kλ^{-k}∫_{M'} θ'ξ'(ω) dHᵏ = R'.action ω.
